title: An update target is a declared sink: upsert 3 orders, then update the same 3 by primary key
proves: a target with the update operation (shop.update) is a declared sink, like a plain or an upsert target: Build counts its routed rows on the sink and does not report 'sink without captured contributors'
the table comes from createTable on the first generate, so the project needs no DDL file; the second generate updates the rows by the primary key
the sink counts the routed rows of both generates (3 inserted + 3 updated = 6); it does not count the rows that the table holds at the end
what the update writes into the table is the engine behaviour that already existed; this scenario proves the Build side only
